name: Atelier Populaire
summary: A workshop of art students and artists who occupied the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris in May 1968. A general assembly voted on each poster. They printed thousands of single-colour silk-screen posters for the strikes and did not sign them.

statement.text: The posters are weapons of the struggle: hang them in the street, not in a gallery, because treating them as decoration or as art destroys their use.
statement.title: Note in the 1969 book of the posters

moves.text: Students and artists who occupied the École des Beaux-Arts started to print posters on a silk-screen press for the May 1968 strikes.

source.title: Wikipedia: Beauty Is in the Street

moves.text: Wikidata dates the end of the workshop to 1968.
